notebook:
PLAN: (1) establish a converged C4/C5 root split and inspect duties/purity; (2) add high-value light and heavy splits, favouring C4/C5/C6 blends where separation is expensive; (3) tune stages/reflux and pressure for profit; (4) compare lean alternatives. Step 1 now.
Initial root at 45 stages, R/B=3, 15% pressure drop aims to split N-butane from isopentane. Feed value is concentrated in C5-C9, so avoid spending early solves on ethane. Premium purity (99%) pays 20%, but expensive-plant costs mean I will compare blend outlets against deep polishing.

note: Build a seven-column blend-oriented backbone: C5 overhead at the root, C3/C4/C5 products above, and C6 paraffin, C6 naphthene, C7, C8 and C9 products below.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) establish a converged C5/C6 root split and full blend backbone; (2) inspect revenue/cost and prune weak light/heavy separations; (3) tune stages/reflux and pressure for profit; (4) compare lean alternatives. Step 1 now.
Initial C4/C5 root was converged but only a diagnostic. The revised root targets C5 overhead, then C4/C5 and C3/C4 splits. Bottoms target the valuable C6 paraffin blend, C6 naphthene blend, and pure C7-C9. Blend recovery avoids costly isomer polishing. Seven moderate columns should give a clear revenue-versus-cost map; premium 99% polishing is secondary in this expensive scenario.

note: Adopt the demonstrated C4-producing backbone, then sharpen the C5/C6 split and the C6-paraffin/heavy split to recover the two largest blend values.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) establish a converged C4/C5 root split and full blend backbone; (2) sharpen the C5 and C6-paraffin cuts; (3) prune weak light/heavy separations; (4) tune stages/reflux and pressure for profit. Step 2 now.
R19 is the useful starting point: root 50/3/2/0.2 and T 40/3/2.5/0.1 already sell the C4 blend for $172.5M/yr. Its B split leaks much C5 into BB and its BB cut leaks C5 plus naphthenes into the C6-paraffin tops. Increase B rectification and moderately increase BB rectification, seeking sellable C5 and C6 blends without my failed seven-column low-purity tree. Avoid isomer polishing initially; blend recovery is the value driver.

note: Sharpen both major blend cuts with stronger rectification; C5 and C6-paraffin recovery dominate the available revenue.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) establish a converged C4/C5 root split and full blend backbone; (2) sharpen the C5 and C6-paraffin cuts; (3) prune weak light/heavy separations; (4) tune stages/reflux and pressure for profit. Step 2 now.
R19 root 50/3/2/0.2 and T 40/3/2.5/0.1 sell C4 for $172.5M. R29 shows low B boil-up damages C5 recovery and adding TT 30/3/2/0.1 can sell C3, so retain those options. Current B 60/5/3 leaves BT only 74% C5 and BB cut leaves BBT 86% C6 paraffin. Test substantially stronger B rectification (90/8/3) and BB rectification (80/5/3); target the two very valuable C5 and C6 blends before polishing lights or heavies. Costs are high, so after achieving purity reduce severity and remove low-value branches.

note: Prune the uneconomic heavy-end separation and add the demonstrated low-cost C3 column, establishing a profitable C3/C4-only baseline.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) establish a profitable light-end core (C3/C4) by pruning loss-making heavy branches; (2) reduce root and light-column severity/cost while preserving blend purity; (3) test only heavy branches with clear positive incremental value; (4) tune final settings. Step 1 now.
All heavy C5/C6 trials are uneconomic: even $598M C5 revenue would not offset root+B costs, and current cuts miss purity. R38 demonstrates TT 30/3/2/0.1 yields $53.8M C3 for $8.1M. With B pruned, root+T+TT should cost $200.5M and earn $226.4M, a positive baseline. Establish it before optimizing.

note: Adopt the demonstrated C3/C4/C5 plant, whose C5 blend adds $526M revenue and raises reward to 0.748, before optimizing its dominant costs.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) adopt the proven profitable C3/C4/C5 backbone; (2) reduce root and C5-splitter cost without losing the 95% C5 threshold; (3) test only high-value heavy cuts with positive incremental economics; (4) tune the best plant. Step 1.
R48 earns $752.1M and costs $424.2M for reward 0.748. Its B column (120/10/3/0.1) produces a 620 mol/s C5 blend worth $525.8M, decisively better than my C3/C4-only baseline. Adopt it unchanged first; then optimize B boil-up/stages/reflux and root severity, since those dominate cost.

note: Reduce the two dominant column duties and sizes moderately; the root C4/C5 cut is easy, while B reflux 8 tests whether the C5 blend remains above 95%.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) adopt the proven profitable C3/C4/C5 backbone; (2) reduce root and C5-splitter cost without losing the 95% C5 threshold; (3) test only high-value heavy cuts with positive incremental economics; (4) tune the best plant. Step 2.
R48/R54 earn about $752M at $424M cost. Root and B dominate ($158.5M and $223.1M). R54 shows B stages 120->110 saves only $0.5M, so duty/reflux matter more than a small stage reduction. R59 confirms severe heavy-end separation is uneconomic and leaves C5 in its C6 cut. Now test root 40/2.2/1.8 and B 100/8/3 to lower operating cost while retaining blend specifications.

note: Restore the best proven C3/C4/C5 design and trim B reflux modestly to reduce its dominant operating cost while retaining C5 blend grade.
notebook: PLAN: (1) use the best proven C3/C4/C5 plant R61 (0.847); (2) lower dominant B duty while preserving C5 grade; (3) optimize the root cut and smaller columns; (4) retain the best valid design. Step 2. R61 uses root 50/3/2 and B110/9/3, yielding $789M revenue and $418M cost. My 40/2.2/1.8 root and B100/8/3 failed every blend. B reflux is near the purity boundary: 10 gives 95% C5, 9 gives 96%; test 8.5 for duty savings. Root is the other major cost and will be tuned only after securing this baseline.

note: Adopt the demonstrated five-column C6-paraffin design, which more than doubles reward by adding a profitable C6 blend and improving C5 recovery.
notebook: PLAN: (1) adopt R77's validated C3/C4/C5/C6-paraffin plant (1.981); (2) optimize the costly B and BB columns while preserving both blend grades; (3) test cheaper root/light-end settings; (4) retain the best valid design. Step 1. R77 adds $750M C6-paraffin revenue for $250M BB cost and recovers more C5, dominating my 0.901 design. B=120/10/3.6 and BB=120/10/5.0 are proven together; avoid R78's higher BB boil-up, which caused n-pentane leakage and lost the blend. Root and light-end columns match my proven backbone.

note: Combine the proven cheaper C6 splitter with the modest B boil-up increase that improved C5 recovery and reduced n-pentane leakage.
notebook: PLAN: (1) adopt R87's cheaper 110/9 BB column (2.102); (2) combine it with B boil-up 3.7, which improved C5 recovery and C6 cleanliness in R81/R86; (3) then tune BB and root/light-end costs; (4) retain best valid. Step 2. R87 gained $44.5M C6 revenue and saved $8.3M versus my current BB. B=3.7 previously added 12 mol/s C5 and reduced C5 leakage into BB; combining these independent improvements should beat either alone. B=110/9 failed for agent-9, so keep B=120/10.

note: Combine the best cheaper C6 splitter with the proven higher B boil-up to recover more C5 while retaining R92's lower cost.
notebook: PLAN: (1) adopt R92's best 100/8.5 BB design (2.166); (2) combine with B boil-up 3.7, which raised C5 recovery at BB=110/9; (3) tune B and root/light-end costs; (4) retain best valid. Step 2. R92 saves $7.8M versus my plant despite B=3.6. At BB=110/9, B=3.7 gained 12 mol/s C5 and $11M revenue, so the combination should improve both revenue and cost baseline.

note: Combine the best low-reflux C6 splitter with B boil-up 3.7: R107 proves BB reflux 8 retains C6 blend grade, while R99 proves the extra boil-up profitably recovers more C5.
notebook: PLAN: (1) combine R107's best BB=100/8 with B boil-up 3.7; (2) tune B and BB around this point for duty/capital savings while keeping C5/C6 blends; (3) test root/light-end cost reductions; (4) retain best valid. Step 1. R107 (B3.6, BB100/8) scores 2.234; R99 shows B3.7 adds $11M C5 revenue for $4.6M cost at BB8.5. At BB8, C6 blend should still qualify and net gain should exceed R107.

note: Combine R109's strong C6 recovery at BB boil-up 6.0 with the proven B boil-up 3.7, which recovered more C5 at modest extra cost.
notebook: PLAN: (1) combine the best BB=6.0 recovery with B boil-up 3.7; (2) tune B/BB for net duty and recovery gains; (3) test root/light-end savings only if worthwhile; (4) retain best valid. Step 1. R109 at B3.6/BB6.0 scores 2.384, gaining $71.8M revenue for $23.1M cost over mine. R99 showed B3.7 adds about $11M C5 revenue for $4.6M cost. Combining should preserve both blend grades and improve the current best.

note: Adopt the best demonstrated backbone and economize the root C4/C5 splitter, whose products have substantial purity headroom.
notebook: PLAN: (1) adopt R125's best 2.458 backbone; (2) reduce root size/reflux because the C4/C5 cut is easy and both products have purity headroom; (3) tune B/BB locally; (4) retain best valid. Step 2. R125 (B3.6, BB7.5/6.0) beats my 2.422 by $15.8M net. Root costs $158.5M/yr despite a sharp C4/C5 split and essentially zero C5 in its tops. Testing 40 stages and reflux 2.5 should cut capital and duty while retaining blend grades; all downstream columns will be resolved on the changed feeds.

note: Combine the two independently beneficial settings: R128's improved C5 recovery at B reflux 9.5 and the extra C6-paraffin recovery from BB boil-up 6.5.
notebook: PLAN: (1) restore R128's best 2.546 backbone; (2) combine its B reflux 9.5 improvement with BB boil-up 6.5, whose extra C6 recovery was independently profitable; (3) tune B/BB locally; (4) retain best valid. Step 2. My 40-stage root failed and sharply degraded all cuts, so abandon root reduction. R128 gains $18.6M C5 revenue and saves $3.7M at B by lowering reflux 10 to 9.5. R130/R133 show BB boil-up 6.5 adds $26.5M C6 revenue for $14.2M cost, net +$12.3M. The two changes affect different splits and should combine for about 2.574.

note: Extend the profitable BB boil-up trend by one modest increment; BBT still has 2% blend-purity headroom for additional C6 recovery.
notebook: PLAN: (1) retain the best 2.610 five-column backbone; (2) test whether BB boil-up above 6.5 still buys C6-paraffin recovery profitably; (3) then tune the dominant B/BB costs conservatively; (4) retain best valid. Step 2. Root reduction failed badly; do not retry. B reflux 9.5 saves money versus 10, but 9.0 fails convergence. Increasing BB boil-up from 6.0 to 6.5 added $26.5M revenue for $14.2M cost. BBT is 97% C6 paraffins, leaving limited but useful headroom, so test 7.0 rather than a larger jump.

note: Combine the two profitable BB adjustments: R146's lower reflux saves cost, while boil-up 7.0 improves C6-paraffin recovery; BBT retains blend-purity headroom.
notebook: PLAN: (1) retain the strongest five-column backbone; (2) optimize BB jointly in reflux/boil-up, since R146 shows reflux 7.0 is profitable at boil-up 6.5; (3) test conservative B/BB size or energy trims only where product grade has headroom; (4) retain best valid. Step 2. Root reduction failed badly; do not retry. B reflux 9.5 saves money versus 10, but 9.0 fails convergence; B 100 stages loses too much C6 recovery. Increasing BB boil-up 6.5→7.0 adds $9.6M net at reflux 7.5. R146's reflux 7.0 at boil-up 6.5 adds $7.7M net. Test their combination: BB reflux 7.0, boil-up 7.0.

Increasing BB boil-up 6.5→7.0 adds $9.6M net at reflux 7.5. R146's reflux 7.0 at boil-up 6.5 adds $7.7M net. Test their combination: BB reflux 7.0, boil-up 7.0.

note: Adopt the best demonstrated backbone and probe one further BB reflux reduction; the C6 blend is near grade, so this directly tests the remaining energy-saving margin.
notebook: PLAN: (1) adopt R164's best 2.837 backbone; (2) probe the BB reflux limit at fixed boil-up 6.5; (3) if purity fails, retain R164 and use remaining solves for modest recovery/cost trade-offs; (4) keep best valid. Step 2. R164 improves over my 2.776 by recovering 33 mol/s more C6 paraffin for only $9.1M/yr extra cost. Its BBT blend is near the 95% limit (about 4% methylcyclopentane plus 1% cyclohexane), so lower reflux may save energy but risks losing the entire C6 product. Root economization failed badly; B reflux 9.0 did not converge and B 100 stages lost recovery. Copy R164 and test BB reflux 5.5 at boil-up 6.5.

PLAN: (1) adopt R177's best 2.888 backbone; (2) cautiously extend BB boil-up to recover more C6 while holding reflux 6.0; (3) retain the best valid and use remaining solves for small profitable adjustments. Step 2. BB reflux 5.5 fails the C6 blend even at boil-up 7.0, so 6.0 is the practical reflux floor. Raising boil-up from 6.5 to 7.0 increased BBT by 30 mol/s and reward by 0.051 despite $8.4M/yr extra cost. Test 7.5: recovery may rise further, but the blend is near 95% and can be lost discontinuously.

note: Restore the best backbone and test coordinated BB rectification: a small reflux increase may remove enough naphthene leakage for boil-up 7.5 to retain blend grade and monetize its extra C6 recovery.
notebook: PLAN: (1) restore R177's 2.888 backbone; (2) test whether modest extra BB rectification makes the higher-recovery 7.5 boil-up cut meet C6 blend grade; (3) if not, retain 6.0/7.0 and spend remaining solves on small cost reductions in B or the root. Step 2. BB reflux 5.5 fails; 6.0/7.0 gives 968 mol/s sellable BBT and reward 2.888. At 6.0/7.5, BBT rises 28 mol/s (~$32M/yr potential) but methylcyclopentane reaches 5% and the blend fails. Extra reflux may restore grade for less than the recovery gain.

note: Adopt the best 2.897 backbone and test coordinated C3-column rectification: lower boil-up should recover more C3 in TTB, while extra reflux should suppress C4 contamination.
notebook: PLAN: (1) adopt R201's 2.897 backbone (BB 6.0/7.1); (2) improve the cheap C3 column by pairing slightly lower boil-up with more reflux, seeking extra C3 recovery without losing 95% blend grade; (3) if it fails, retain R201 and test modest stage/cost reductions. Step 2. R201 shows BB 7.1 is the recovery optimum: 7.2 crosses the blend cliff. At 6.5/7.5 my BBT remains sellable but cost wipes out its gain. TT currently strands about 76 mol/s C3 in TTT; TT costs only $8.1M/yr, so coordinated rectification may recover it cheaply.

note: Add a cyclohexane/heptane splitter to monetize the large unsold BBB stream as a C6-naphthene blend; its residual light content is only about 5%, so a moderate column should reach blend grade.
notebook: PLAN: (1) retain the 2.903 blend backbone; (2) monetize BBB by splitting its C6 naphthenes from C7+; (3) tune that split if needed, then use remaining solves for small proven improvements. Step 2. TT rectification gained only $4M revenue for $1.3M cost. BBB contains about 224 mol/s methylcyclopentane+cyclohexane, worth roughly $330M/yr as a 95% blend, while its residual lights are only about 5%; a sharp cyclohexane/heptane cut should therefore add substantial profit. BB 7.1 is the recovery cliff optimum and stage reductions on B/BB are catastrophic.

note: Sharpen the BBB naphthene/C7 split with much stronger rectification and lower boil-up; the first attempt leaked both heptane and hexane into the tops.
notebook: PLAN: (1) retain the 2.903 blend backbone; (2) monetize BBB by splitting its C6 naphthenes from C7+; (3) tune that split if needed, then use remaining solves for small proven improvements. Step 3. TT rectification gained only $4M revenue for $1.3M cost; R216 shows TT 30/4.0/1.6 is best at 2.909. The first BBB split at 60/4/2 was far too broad: top only 61% naphthenes with 22% heptane and 15% hexane. BBB still contains about 214 mol/s naphthenes worth roughly $320M/yr. Test much stronger rectification and lower boil-up (100/10/0.8) to reject both heptane and residual hexane. BB 7.1 is the recovery cliff optimum and stage reductions on B/BB are catastrophic.

note: Restore the 2.912 backbone and test a balanced BBB naphthene splitter: more boil-up than the stripping-limited attempt, with more stages and reflux to suppress heptane leakage.
notebook: PLAN: (1) restore the best five-column blend backbone and its improved C3 settings; (2) make one final, balanced attempt to monetize BBB as C6 naphthenes; (3) revert if it does not beat 2.912. Step 2. The 100/10/0.8 BBB split was far too stripping-limited: only 64 mol/s overhead at 72% naphthene grade. Earlier 60/4/2 gave more overhead but 22% heptane. Use 120/12/1.5 to increase overhead recovery while retaining strong rectification. Potential gross value is about $320M/yr, enough to justify a substantial column if grade is reached. BB 7.1 is the recovery cliff optimum; B/BB stage cuts are catastrophic. TT 30/4.5/1.5 is the demonstrated 2.912 best.

note: Combine R235's profitable higher-pressure-drop C6 splitter with R237's independently improved C3 recovery settings; their benefits should be additive.
notebook: PLAN: (1) remove the unprofitable BBB naphthene splitter and restore the best five-column blend backbone; (2) combine independently proven BB-pressure and C3-recovery gains; (3) use remaining solves only for small, evidence-backed refinements. Step 2. R235 shows BB dp 0.2 improves C6 recovery by $18M/yr for $11.6M extra cost, beating dp 0.1. R237 shows TT 30/5.0/1.4 adds about $2M/yr C3 revenue for $0.8M cost. Combining them should exceed 2.926 if effects are additive. B dp 0.2 fails convergence, so do not repeat it. B and BB stage reductions are catastrophic; BB boil-up 7.1 is the recovery-cliff optimum. BBB split attempts all reduced reward.

note: Extend the profitable BB pressure trend to 0.30 while retaining the best demonstrated C3 settings; dp 0.25 still gave a positive net gain, and the two improvements are independent.
notebook: PLAN: (1) retain the proven five-column blend backbone; (2) combine independently proven BB-pressure and C3-recovery gains; (3) spend the last solves on the continuing BB-pressure trend. Step 3. BB dp 0.2 improved reward versus 0.1, and R245 shows dp 0.25 adds another $1.8M/yr net. Test dp 0.30 while retaining TT 30/5.0/1.4, which beats R245's TT settings by about $1.2M/yr net. B dp 0.2 fails convergence. B and BB stage reductions are catastrophic; BB boil-up 7.1 is the recovery-cliff optimum. BBB split attempts all reduced reward.

note: Bracket the BB pressure optimum with one final higher-pressure test; gains from 0.25 to 0.30 were small, so 0.35 should reveal whether the trend has turned.
